channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Flávio: Judiciário deve ser 'consertado' e STF não pode ser 'delegacia '
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, PL presidential candidate, stated that the Judiciary needs reform and that the STF should not act as a 'police station'. During an event in Americana, SP, he signaled openness to changes in the Judicial Power.

item.title: Candidatos fazem últimos atos de campanha na véspera da eleição em Apucarana
item.description: Candidates held their final campaign events on Saturday morning in downtown Apucarana, with strong supporter turnout and street activity. The election race heated up with car horns and flags filling the central area ahead of Sunday's vote. The atmosphere reflected high political engagement and voter anticipation.

item.title: TSE verifica urnas e reafirma integridade da disputa pela Presidência
item.description: The TSE conducted a ceremony on Saturday, 3, to verify the integrity and authenticity of the electoral systems, ensuring the mechanisms used in the 2026 presidential election are regularly inspected. This measure aims to guarantee the transparency and credibility of the electoral process.

item.title: Após tensão com PM, Lula faz último ato de rua: 'Paulista não é da direita'
item.description: President Lula held his final campaign rally on Paulista Avenue following an initial tension with military police over the walking route. The event proceeded without further incidents, with Lula emphasizing that the region does not belong to the right. The campaign closes with an appeal for progressive voting.

item.title: Brasil elege próximo Congresso, que pode definir destino de Jair Bolsonaro
item.description: In addition to electing the president, Brazilian voters choose state and federal deputies and senators for a National Congress that may influence the fate of former president Jair Bolsonaro, currently imprisoned for an attempted coup.

item.title: Ciro Gomes diz que apoio de Flávio Bolsonaro é 'irrelevante' no Ceará
item.description: Ciro Gomes (PSDB), running for Ceará governor, dismissed support from Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) as irrelevant to his campaign. The statement follows a rift between Flávio and former first lady Michelle Bolsonaro over alliance strategy.

item.title: Caetano, Gil e Chico Buarque lançam jingle pela reeleição de Lula
item.description: Musicians Caetano Veloso, Gilberto Gil, and Chico Buarque released a samba jingle supporting Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's re-election, highlighting the importance of conscious voting and defending national sovereignty. The lyrics also criticize potential foreign interference, particularly from the United States, in the Brazilian campaign.

item.title: Proibição das bets pode estar com dias contados; decisão está com Luiz Fux
item.description: Supreme Court minister Luiz Fux is reviewing a request to suspend the Provisional Measure banning online betting, threatening the government's oversight efforts. The deadline for the Attorney General's Office to respond is within 72 hours, with a ruling possible at any time.

item.title: Quem são todos os candidatos a deputado federal pelo Rio de Janeiro (RJ) nas eleições 2026
item.description: Over 12.8 million eligible voters in Rio de Janeiro will elect 46 federal deputies from 793 candidates, with 28 disqualified by the Electoral Court. The election takes place in a single round on October 4, with seats distributed proportionally based on the electoral quotient among parties.

item.title: Goldman Sachs diz que próximo presidente herdará dívida de 87% do PIB
item.description: Goldman Sachs projects that the next Brazilian president will inherit public debt of 86.9% of GDP in 2027, with 1.2% economic growth and 4.5% inflation. The report highlights challenges such as deficits above 8% of GDP and lack of clear fiscal strategies from candidates Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Trump volta a prometer US$ 5 mil se republicanos vencerem eleições
item.description: Donald Trump promised $5,000 per adult if Republicans win the midterm elections for the House and Senate, reinforcing his campaign while criticizing Biden's administration. He emphasized economic success under Republican leadership and avoided commenting directly on Flávio Bolsonaro. Polls suggest Democrats may regain control of the House.

item.title: País sairá das urnas com feridas abertas, em crise institucional e com cenário adverso para o eleito
item.description: Regardless of the winner, either Lula or Flávio Bolsonaro, Brazil faces institutional crisis, Supreme Court erosion and polarization, requiring prioritization of legal investigations over governance.

item.title: Wilson Pedroso na Crusoé: Padroeira vira munição de campanha
item.description: Wilson Pedroso and the 2026 campaign exploit devotion to Our Lady of Aparecida as political ammunition, with both sides weaponizing the religious symbol in the electoral race. The fake news spread on September 24th illustrates how Brazil's patron saint has become a target of digital manipulation for electoral purposes.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro fala em ‘Libertar o Brasil’ em motociata no interior de SP
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro concluded his campaign with a motorcycle parade in São Paulo alongside Tarcísio de Freitas, attacking the STF and betting on first-round victory. He labeled the Supreme Court as 'police station' and criticized Lula's allies.

item.title: Douglas Ruas vai à Baixada na véspera da eleição e endurece críticas a adversários e ‘traidores’
item.description: Douglas Ruas escalated criticisms against opponents and 'traitors' during campaign rallies in the Baixada region, as Eduardo Paes leads voter intentions. Allies who abandoned the ticket were mocked, and Ruas called for votes for himself and Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Em SP, na véspera da votação, Lula e Flávio falam em vencer no 1º turno
item.description: On the eve of the first round of the 2026 presidential elections, Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro spoke in São Paulo, expressing confidence in victory. Lula emphasized the fight against organized crime, while Flávio claimed he could win like Governor Tarcísio.

item.title: Não interfiram em nossas eleições, dizem centrais sindicais aos EUA
item.description: Brazilian labor unions criticized the suspension of U.S. consular services ahead of the first round of elections, calling it an unnecessary and politically motivated measure. They defended democracy and Brazil's sovereignty, emphasizing that the electoral process is a global reference for modernity and democratic practice.

item.title: ‘Posso até apoiar Ruas, contrariado’, diz Garotinho, se seus votos forem validados e eleição no Rio for ao segundo turno
item.description: Following the revocation of a injunction that kept his candidacy for Rio governor, Anthony Garotinho stated he may support Douglas Ruas in a runoff, if his votes are validated. Otherwise, he urged voters to cast ballots for number 10 as a form of protest. The ruling does not end the legal dispute, as the TSE will still review the appeal against the candidacy rejection by the TRE-RJ.

item.title: Lula diz se sentir “menino de 15” e manda perguntar a Janja
item.description: During a campaign rally in São Paulo, President Lula, 80, said he feels like a '15-year-old boy' and urged voters aged 70+ to vote for their children, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren. The event included Haddad, Alckmin, Marina Silva, and Simone Tebet, and briefly faced police tension.

item.title: Eduardo Leite corre sem camisa em campanha por candidato no RS
item.description: Rio Grande do Sul Governor Eduardo Leite (PSD) posted a photo on Instagram showing him shirtless while running with the campaign flag of Gabriel Souza (MDB) and Ernani Polo (PSD) for state government. The post received positive comments from followers praising the governor's physique. Leite, serving his second term, supports Gabriel Souza, his current vice-governor, as the candidate for state succession.

item.title: TSE faz teste final de sistemas e emite zerézima
item.description: The TSE conducted final tests of the electoral systems and issued the Zerézima, ensuring transparency and security for the first round of the 2026 Elections. The procedure confirms no votes are registered before voting begins and validates the integrity of software used in the voting machines.

item.title: Brasil 4 x 0 Índia: confira os gols da goleada do Brasil em Calcutá
item.description: The Brazilian National Team defeated India 4-0 in a friendly match during the FIFA International Break, with two goals from Samuel Lino and one each from Estêvão and Pedro. The game was played in Kolkata, concluding Brazil's October fixtures as they prepare to face Japan and Singapore in November.

item.title: Como saber onde votar nas eleições de 2026? Confira seu local de votação
item.description: The Brazilian Electoral Justice provides, via the e-Título app and TSE website, information about polling stations and routes to reach them. Over 158 million Brazilians are eligible to vote in the first round of the 2026 elections, scheduled for October 4th, from 8 AM to 5 PM (Brasília time).

item.title: Só falta aparecer quem participou da orgia, diz Lula sobre Master
item.description: Lula criticized opponents in the Master case during a walk in São Paulo with running mates. He targeted Daniel Vorcaro, a 'gang' in Social Security, and hinted at an 'orgy' of participants. There was a clash with the police before the event, which proceeded along Paulista Avenue.

item.title: Ao vivo: TSE realiza teste de integridade das urnas eletrônicas
item.description: On Saturday (Oct 3, 2026) at 2 PM, the TSE conducts an integrity test of the electronic voting machines for the first-round elections on Sunday (Oct 4). The audit procedure involves pre-filling paper ballots and verifying that the electronic count matches the physical records. The audit will also take place Sunday during the official vote, including biometric testing and oversight by the Federal Court of Accounts.

item.title: Haddad diz que Ricardo Nunes tentou impedir caminhada de Lula em SP
item.description: Fernando Haddad accused Ricardo Nunes of trying to block Lula's march in São Paulo. The military police denied interference, stating they acted for safety and traffic flow.

item.title: Ex-embaixador dos EUA considera “erro grave” contestar eleições do Brasil
item.description: Former U.S. ambassador to Brazil Thomas Shannon called it a 'grave error' for any country to challenge Brazil's election results without clear fraud evidence. He emphasized the credibility of Brazil's electoral system. His remarks come amid tensions between the Trump and Lula administrations, with protests in the U.S. over the Brazilian election.

item.title: Lula diz disputar contra ‘chefes de quadrilha’ e ‘crime organizado’ em ato na Paulista
item.description: At his final campaign rally before the first round, President Lula said he is running against 'gang leaders' and 'organized crime', without naming his opponent Flávio Bolsonaro. He emphasized voter participation and defended changes to the financial system and credit card issuance. The speech featured political accusations and calls for voter mobilization.

item.title: Na reta final, Cury pede que brasileiro não tenha medo de caminhar
item.description: In the final stretch of the campaign, Augusto Cury released a letter to Brazilians via Instagram, highlighting the growth from 1% to 11% in polls and encouraging voters not to fear the proposed path. He emphasized that Brazil was not born to live in a dead end and stressed the importance of voting in the first round. Cury requested votes for number 70, promising that the ballots will record the day the country returned to pursuing peace and dreaming big.

item.title: Toffoli manda rádio e TV do CE compensarem propaganda eleitoral
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Dias Toffoli ordered radio and TV stations in Ceará to compensate for unaird electoral advertising benefiting the 'Ceará Forte, do Lado Certo' coalition. The ruling corrects failures in airing additional time granted to Elmano de Freitas (PT) after Toffoli annulled response rights granted to Ciro Gomes (PSDB). Stations must broadcast the accumulated time by Saturday (October 3rd), facing a fine of BRL 100,000 otherwise.

item.title: Lula promete ocupar Avenida Paulista no domingo e faz apelo para idosos irem votar
item.description: Lula closed his campaign for the first round with a walk through Rua Augusta in São Paulo, promising to occupy Avenida Paulista on Sunday after vote count, if elected. He made a special appeal for voters aged 70 and over to participate, emphasizing the importance of voting for future generations. The event also featured Haddad, Alckmin, Marina Silva, and Tebet.

item.title: Michelle rebate Janja em último ato de campanha ao Senado e elogia Nikolas: 'Piá do nosso coração'
item.description: In her final campaign rally for the Senate, Michelle Bolsonaro countered First Lady Janja da Silva's criticisms of Deputy Nikolas Ferreira, calling him 'the kid of our heart' and defending him against accusations. The exchange between both sides began after Lula made remarks about preventive exams, which Nikolas took out of context on social media.

item.title: Gilmar derruba direito de resposta de Jerônimo em vídeos de ACM Neto na Bahia
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes overturned decisions from the Bahia Electoral Court requiring APC Neto to broadcast response videos from Jeronimo Rodrigues. The ruling suspends the obligation for reply content, emphasizing freedom of expression and press freedom during the electoral campaign. The case addresses reply rights and the impact of audiovisual content in the Bahian election.

item.title: Exatus/RN: Allyson oscila de 44,1% para 43,2%; Cadu tem 24,4% e Álvaro, 22,2%
item.description: Exatus/RN poll shows Allyson Bezerra (União Brasil) leading with 43.26%, followed by Cadu de Lula (PT) at 24.42% and Álvaro Dias (PL) at 22.22%. Voting intentions oscillated among the three gubernatorial candidates in Rio Grande do Norte.

item.title: Argentina lidera número de eleitores brasileiros na América Latina
item.description: Argentina leads the Brazilian electoral college in Latin America with 13,138 eligible voters, followed by Paraguay with 9,225. Over 90,000 Brazilians live in Argentina, but only 13,000 are registered to vote in the 2026 elections. To avoid queues, the consulate will assign voters to sections before voting.

item.title: A nova proposta de Renan Santos para debate com Flávio
item.description: Renan Santos (Missão) challenged Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) to a debate on Saturday, proposing to withdraw his candidacy and support the senator in the first round if defeated. The offer was made via social media, without a specific time or location. The move aims to boost Santos' campaign visibility.

item.title: Confira a agenda dos candidatos a presidente no último dia de campanha
item.description: On the final day of campaigning before the first round of the 2026 elections, the main candidates held public events in the Southeast region. Lula concluded his campaign in São Paulo with a walk alongside allies such as Geraldo Alckmin and Marina Silva, while Flávio Bolsonaro split his time between events in São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro. Other candidates, including Augusto Cury, Renan Santos, and Ronaldo Caiado, also held events in various cities across the country.

item.title: Lula termina campanha no primeiro turno sem ir ao estado de Hugo Motta
item.description: Lula concludes the first-round campaign without visiting Paraíba, where there is division among allies supporting his re-election. The decision aims to avoid conflicts between local political groups, especially after the president's support for figures like João Azevêdo and Veneziano Vital, causing discomfort with Hugo Motta. The strategy was also adjusted in Pernambuco and Alagoas due to local influences.

item.title: Os movimentos de Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro nessa reta final de campanha
item.description: Lula concludes his campaign in São Paulo, while Flávio Bolsonaro wraps up in Americana, reflecting a polarized climate. Despite mutual accusations, polls keep the candidates neck-and-neck.

item.title: Em 49 dias, Lula fez 26 atos de campanha
item.description: President Lula conducted 26 campaign events over 49 days, focusing on the three largest electoral colleges: São Paulo (5 events), Minas Gerais and Rio de Janeiro (4 each). Despite this focus, polls show his main rival, Flávio Bolsonaro, leading in less-visited regions such as the North and Center-West.

item.title: Lula e Flávio já gastaram mais de 70% do teto no 1º turno
item.description: Lula and Flávio have already used over 70% of the electoral spending cap in the first round, with expenses of R$65.69 million and R$62.95 million, respectively. However, Flávio leads in amounts actually paid, with R$41.31 million against Lula's R$34.71 million. Lula's main expenses are related to communication, including a R$31 million payment to Delta3 Communication and Projects.

item.title: Lula e Flávio concentram campanha nos 3 maiores colégios eleitorais
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro focused much of their campaign in the Southeast, particularly in São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, and Minas Gerais, which hold 42% of Brazil's electorate. Flávio made 44 campaign trips, with 54.5% going to these three states, while Lula held 13 events in the region and campaigned across 14 states. Both candidates' strategies reflect the electoral weight of the Southeast, as Lula also leveraged official presidential trips to support his campaign.

item.title: Eleições 2026: por que as últimas pesquisas consideram os votos válidos
item.description: The 2026 electoral polls now emphasize valid votes to assess first-round victory potential. This aligns the polling data with the official ballot calculation, which excludes blank and null votes.

item.title: Lula tem 45,88% contra 45,01% de Flávio no 2º turno, diz pesquisa
item.description: A survey by the Franca Institute released on October 3, 2026 shows a technical tie between Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in a potential second-round runoff, with 45.88% and 45.01% respectively, within the 2.2-percentage-point margin of error. The study, registered with the Electoral Supreme Court under number BR-02928/2026, was conducted between September 28 and October 2, 2026 with 2,000 respondents and cost R$80,000.

item.title: Por que Daniel Vorcaro e o Careca do INSS podem votar e Jair Bolsonaro não?
item.description: Provisional prisoners like Daniel Vorcaro and the Careca do INSS retain voting rights in 2026, while Jair Bolsonaro is ineligible due to a final conviction. The Anti-Face Law, effective since 2023, bans voting by all prisoners, but will only be fully applied in upcoming elections due to the electoral annulity principle.

item.title: O protagonismo do STF na eleição
item.description: The 2026 election unfolds with the Supreme Federal Court in the spotlight, sparking controversies that also affect the Superior Electoral Court. Reports reveal judicial backstage dynamics and their impact on the judiciary's institutional image.

item.title: Lula tem 43,9% e Flávio Bolsonaro 40,5% dos votos válidos no 1º turno, diz Instituto França
item.description: Instituto França poll shows Lula at 43.9% and Flávio Bolsonaro at 40.5% in the first round, maintaining a technical tie. In the second round, the gap narrows to less than one percentage point. Together, they account for 78.1% of voting intentions.

item.title: Trineto de Dom Pedro II cita Nossa Senhora na véspera das eleições
item.description: Dom Bertrand de Orleans e Bragança, a member of the imperial family, issued a statement urging Brazilians to vote according to natural law without endorsing any candidate. He closed his speech invoking Our Lady of Aparecida amid a clash between the campaigns of Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro over the national patron saint. The controversy involved accusations of fake news regarding Flávio's alleged plan to remove Mary's title as patroness.

item.title: "Motociata da Liberdade" reúne eleitores de Celina, Flávio e Michelle no DF
item.description: Supporters of Celina Leão, Flávio Bolsonaro, and Michelle Bolsonaro held the 'Freedom Motorcycle Parade' in DF, showing support for the candidates and criticizing the federal government. The event gathered at Granja do Torto and ended at Mané Garrincha Stadium.

item.title: Renan Santos diz que continuará usando Bete Balanço após repúdio de Frejat
item.description: Presidential candidate Renan Santos stated he will continue using the parody 'Bete Balanço' in his campaign, despite musician Frejat's repudiation, as Frejat co-wrote the original song with Cazuza.
